issues: Targets: the draft stays within the ‘summary only’ boundary, but the phrasing creates a material risk of implying overall 1.5°C/Paris alignment beyond the evidenced Scope 1–2 target.
Covenant usage: one statement extends covenant application beyond what is evidenced (mortgage flood exposure).

IFRS S1 connectivity: connections between strategy and metrics/targets/risk management are mentioned, but could be made slightly more explicit (e.g., how financed-emissions metrics and high-carbon exposure concretely drive limits, pricing, or sector strategy decisions). This is a minor completeness issue rather than a missing-evidence issue.
available_evidence_omitted: Scenario methodology summaries by scenario type (orderly/disorderly/hot house), including the stated scope emphasis for disorderly scenarios (automotive and energy manufacturing sub-portfolio) and the carbon-price mapping basis (IEA NZE 2050 trajectory for orderly).

Opportunity-level breakdown of the EUR 465.0m estimated revenue impact by opportunity type (green loan growth, sustainable bond underwriting, transition advisory, renewable energy project finance, operational energy efficiency) and their time horizons/confidence levels.
unsupported_claims: “Scope 1 and 2 emissions reduction target set using a 1.5°C-aligned framework” (supported as SBTi 1.5°C for Scope 1–2), but the draft also implies broader “1.5°C-aligned” positioning without clarifying it is limited to Scope 1–2.

“net-zero ambitions for financed emissions set using an NZBA framework” (NZBA is evidenced for financed-emissions intensity target and a 2050 net-zero target; “net-zero ambitions for financed emissions” is slightly imprecise versus the evidenced target types).

“transition-related covenants … in those portfolios where flood and other physical risks are most material” (the evidence links covenants to the mortgage flood exposure risk; extending to “other physical risks” is not evidenced).
material_unsupported_claims: “Scope 1 and 2 emissions reduction target set using a 1.5°C-aligned framework” used alongside “net-zero ambitions for financed emissions … NZBA framework” risks being read as overall Paris/1.5°C alignment of the Bank’s strategy. The evidence boundary explicitly cautions against Paris-alignment overclaims; the draft should explicitly confine 1.5°C alignment to the Scope 1–2 target only and avoid implying bank-wide Paris alignment.

“transition-related covenants … where flood and other physical risks are most material” over-extends beyond the evidenced covenant use for the mortgage flood exposure risk; remove “other physical risks” or specify only the evidenced context.
minor_wording_to_tighten: “value-chain perspective that covers upstream funding providers” (the value-chain map evidence covers upstream suppliers and upstream capital providers generally; “funding providers” is plausible but should be phrased as “capital providers/funding markets” to avoid implying a mapped node not shown).

“stranded asset and revenue-at-risk estimates … used to inform strategic planning horizons and risk appetite” (risk appetite linkage is supported; “strategic planning horizons” is plausible but could be tightened to “strategic planning and capital planning” to match the scenario narrative).

“high-carbon sector exposure is 35.5% of the loan book” (numerically consistent with the portfolio metrics, but clarify it refers to the lending book/total loans to avoid ambiguity with other balance-sheet exposures).
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: “Only target summary information is currently disclosed; further details are provided in the Metrics and targets section.”
“The Bank does not currently disclose a standalone transition plan document or the detailed macroeconomic, policy or customer-behaviour assumptions and dependencies that would underpin such a plan.”
“The Bank does not currently disclose a separate, detailed assessment of climate-related impacts on its overall business model architecture, nor quantified trade-offs…”
“Current-period financial effects have not yet been mapped in detail to specific financial statement line items… [and] does not currently disclose quantified potential adjustments…”
Scenario outputs repeatedly described as “modelled estimates… not realised or forecast losses.”
Opportunity revenue impacts described as “estimates… not assured outcomes.”
“The Bank has not yet quantified full operational adaptation capacity across all business lines.”
